subjects.introduction: A call to action begins with a recognized moment. Bahá’u’lláh describes a Day in which every seeing eye is asked to behold, every hearing ear to listen and every tongue to proclaim, and He warns that even words can become veils between a person and the deed they point toward. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks why the friends are quenched and silent when they could shine like candles and move like soft breezes across the world, yet he also tells a weary soul to rest, makes a journey depend on permission, and insists that a cry raised for God means teaching with wisdom, never with weapons. Answering such a call means first clearing one’s own house, then speaking with kindness and judgment, then joining others in service to humanity according to capacity and means. The road runs on into effort and striving, into teaching the Cause, and into the praise and encouragement that keeps a tired worker going. Prayer carries the work when strength runs out, and the lasting question is whether conviction has become visible in a useful deed.

What would count as evidence that conviction has changed a life? How can self-examination remain connected with responsibility to others?
